results.title: Methodologies and Ethical Considerations in Phishing Research: A Comprehensive Review
results.content: By identifying the types of experiments being conducted and the ethical and legal guidelines that should be followed, researchers can ensure that their studies are conducted safely and responsibly, while also advancing our understanding of how to safeguard against phishing attacks. The existing framework of conducting experiments in phishing research is consisting of three approaches: Survey studies, Laboratory studies and Field studies are the three basic methods used in phishing research with the latter being the most morally and legally questionable, but at the same time also the most ecologically valid [13]. R. Finn [14] summarize the phishing experiments ethics by stating that these “… can be conducted ethically if risks are minimized, confidentiality and privacy are protected, potential participants have an opportunity to opt out of the research before it begins, and human subjects are debriefed after their participation ends.”. Field studies in the contrary may raise serious ethical concerns because in this type of experiment, researchers simulate a real phishing attack while observing the participants' reactions to it, involving deception about the true goal of the research [13]. When planning phishing studies, academic researchers must deal with the requirement that any experiments are not only ethically conducted but also evaluated and authorized by their Institutional Review Board (IRB). By identifying the types of experiments being conducted and the ethical and legal guidelines that should be followed, researchers can ensure that their studies are conducted safely and responsibly, while additionally enhancing our comprehension of strategies to counter phishing attempts. The following selection criteria were employed to identify, analyze and organize the relevant literature from the search query: research articles must be published in conferences, books, or journals, they should describe existing phishing experiments as well provide information on the ethical and procedural aspects during the experimental setting up, include references to the “Institutional Review Board” or “IRB”, “Informed Consent” and “Deception” and have been published during 2018-2023. In cases where phishing experiments necessitate deceit and relinquishment of informed agreement, Institutional Review Boards (IRBs) must initially endorse such experiments considering that the projected advantages of the study will surpass the expected hazards, the study fulfills specific standards outlined in the regulations governing research on human subjects and necessitate that the researchers provide a post-experiment briefing to the participants.

results.title: Institutional Review Board (IRB) Approval - One UNC Clinical Research
results.content: Home / Playbooks / My Study Lifecycle / Study Start-Up / Institutional Review Board (IRB) Approval. # Institutional Review Board (IRB) Approval. The **UNC Institutional Review Boards (IRBs)** are committees established to protect the rights, welfare, and safety of human subjects involved in research. The IRBs ensures that all research complies with ethical principles, federal and state regulations, and institutional policies. + UNC IRB Consent Form Templates. + Preparing the Informed Consent Form (ICF). + Obtaining Informed Consent from Adult Research Participants. * Recruitment materials (e.g., study flyers, scripts for contacting potential participants). * Study instruments (e.g., laboratory tests, medical devices, software to be used, etc.). * Site-specific documentation (e.g., contracts with external sites (BAAs, DUAs, MOUs), investigator brochure, information on facilities to be used, etc.). 2. Submit the required documents using the IRB Informational System (IRBIS). 3. Address all IRB comments promptly. Learn More: Informed Consent Process. ### Office of Human Research Ethics (OHRE). The Office of Human Research Ethics (OHRE) is responsible for ethical and regulatory oversight of research at UNC-Chapel Hill that involves human subjects. The OHRE administers, supports, and guides the work of the Institutional Review Boards (IRBs) and all related activities. Any research involving human subjects proposed by faculty, staff, or students must be reviewed and approved by an IRB before research may begin, and before related grants may be funded. UNC-Chapel Hill has six Institutional Review Boards (IRBs) to manage and review the wide range of research conducted at the institution. The UNC IRB is responsible for the following:. + Ensures research protocols are compliant with ethical standards, such as respect for persons, beneficence, and justice. + Reviews informed consent documents to ensure clarity and voluntariness. + Ensures risks to participants are minimized and justified by potential benefits. + Reviews compliance with UNC policies and state laws. + Conducts continuing review for ongoing studies (when applicable). * UNC IRBIS Online Submission Guide. * UNC IRBIS Online Submission FAQ. * IRB Training and Education Resources. * General Inquiries: irb\_questions@unc.edu. * Concerns for Research Subjects: irb\_subjects@unc.edu. * Reliance Agreements, Commercial IRBs, Single IRB, Smart IRB, and Independent Investigators: irbreliance@unc.edu. * IRBIS Technical Help Desk: IRBIS@unc.edu. * IRB Membership: irbmembers@unc.edu.

results.title: Informed Consent: The Requirements for Informed Consent (Series #1) | 2025 | IRB Blog | Institutional Review Board | Teachers College, Columbia University
results.content: ## This TC IRB Blog Series will lay out the basic and common components of Informed consent in research with human subjects. Consent processes may vary, but they always include: (1) information disclosure; (2) assessment of competency to consent and the participants’ ability to make a decision, and (3) emphasize the voluntary nature of the decision to participate in research. The ethical and legal validity of volunteering for a study is dependent upon the consent process which requires dialogue, information sharing, or negotiation between researcher and prospective study participant. Researchers are responsible for developing consent forms for information-sharing that emphasize the **voluntary** nature of study participation. The consenting process includes a researcher's assessment of the cognitive competency of the prospective participant to make a decision and includes documentation of the individuals’ decision to agree to volunteer for the study (Kodama Muscente, 2022). All consent materials must comply with both the legal and ethical requirements to obtain informed consent to be approved by TC IRB for use in human subjects research.

results.title: Ethical Considerations in Legal Research | Advanced Legal Research Class Notes
results.content: ## 8.3 Ethical Considerations in Legal Research. # 8.3 Ethical Considerations in Legal Research. 8.3 Ethical Considerations in Legal Research. Legal research involves more than just finding information. From protecting client confidentiality to avoiding conflicts of interest, researchers must stay vigilant. Ethical considerations in legal research extend beyond individual cases. Researchers must maintain objectivity, use appropriate methods, and recognize personal biases. Understanding and applying ethical guidelines is crucial for conducting responsible and reliable legal research. ## Ethical Issues in Legal Research. * Legal research often involves accessing and handling sensitive or confidential information. * Researchers must take precautions to protect the confidentiality and security of this information. ### Ethical Research Methods. * The use of certain research methods can raise ethical concerns. * Researchers should carefully consider the ethical implications of their chosen methods. * Plagiarism, or the unattributed use of others' ideas or work product, is a serious ethical violation in legal research and writing. ## Applying Ethical Guidelines to Legal Research. * Researchers should familiarize themselves with the relevant rules and ensure their conduct aligns with these ethical standards. * Jurisdictions often have specific rules or opinions governing the ethical use of online research tools, databases, and social media in gathering information for cases. * Researchers should stay up-to-date on the ethical rules and opinions in their jurisdiction and consult with colleagues or supervisors when questions arise. * Institutional Review Boards (IRBs) set ethical guidelines for research involving human subjects. + IRBs review research proposals to ensure they meet ethical standards for informed consent, privacy, and minimization of risks. * Legal researchers should be aware of IRB requirements and seek guidance when their work may constitute human subjects research. * These principles provide a useful framework for legal researchers to evaluate the ethical dimensions of their work and make responsible decisions. ## Client Confidentiality in Legal Research. * Researchers must take reasonable precautions to safeguard client information. * Researchers should clearly mark privileged documents and take steps to maintain the confidentiality of attorney-client communications. * Researchers should consult with supervising attorneys before sharing any client information with outside parties. ## Recognizing Personal Biases in Legal Research.
